title: Budget 2026-27, repo rate holds and a strong Q1 GDP print
text:
Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman presented the Union Budget for 2026-27 in Parliament on 1 February 2026, a Sunday, the first time a Budget was delivered on that day in independent India. It was her ninth consecutive Budget. She set the fiscal deficit target for 2026-27 at 4.3 per cent of GDP, slightly below the 4.4 per cent revised estimate for 2025-26, and said she had fulfilled her 2021-22 commitment to bring the deficit below 4.5 per cent of GDP by 2025-26. The Budget raised capital expenditure to about Rs 12.2 lakh crore and projected the Centre's debt at 55.6 per cent of GDP, with the stated aim of moving towards around 50 per cent by March 2031. Total expenditure was estimated at Rs 53.47 lakh crore, or 13.6 per cent of GDP.

Five days later, on 6 February 2026, the Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Committee, chaired by Governor Sanjay Malhotra, kept the policy repo rate unchanged at 5.25 per cent with a neutral stance. It was the Governor's first policy review after the Budget. The Committee repeated the decision on 5 June 2026, citing elevated crude oil prices, a weaker rupee and monsoon concerns. At its meeting of 3 to 5 August 2026, the MPC voted unanimously to hold the rate at 5.25 per cent once more and retained the neutral stance. The RBI projected real GDP growth of 6.7 per cent and consumer price inflation of 5.0 per cent for 2026-27. The repo rate had been lowered by a cumulative 125 basis points during 2025 before the pause began.

The central bank's growth projection was overtaken by official data on 31 August 2026. The National Statistical Office reported that India's real GDP grew 7.8 per cent in April-June 2026, the first quarter of 2026-27, against a Reuters poll median of 7.1 per cent and the RBI's own estimate of 7 per cent. Real GDP was put at Rs 81.36 lakh crore, while nominal GDP rose 10.3 per cent to Rs 88.27 lakh crore. Gross value added grew 8.2 per cent, led by services, and gross fixed capital formation rose 11.9 per cent, a sign that public investment was feeding through. ICRA raised its full-year forecast to 7.1 per cent from 6.7 per cent, though analysts cautioned that high crude prices and inflation remained risks.

The MPC met again from 5 to 7 October 2026. Economists were divided on whether the Committee would hold or raise rates, which would have been the first increase since February 2023.

questions.q: The Union Budget presented in Parliament each year is constitutionally described as the 'annual financial statement'. Which Article of the Constitution of India requires it to be laid before both Houses?
questions.explanation: Article 112(1) requires the President to cause an estimate of receipts and expenditure for each financial year, the annual financial statement, to be laid before both Houses.

questions.q: The National Statistical Office, which released the Q1 2026-27 GDP estimate, functions under which Union Ministry?
options: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
questions.explanation: GDP estimates are released by the NSO under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).

questions.assertion: Salaries of Supreme Court judges are not subject to a vote by the Lok Sabha when the Budget is passed.
questions.reason: Such expenditure is charged on the Consolidated Fund of India under Article 112(3).
questions.explanation: Article 112(3) lists charged expenditure, including salaries of Supreme Court judges and debt charges, which is not voted upon; so R correctly explains A.

list1: III. CPI inflation target set for the MPC
IV. Statutory basis for constituting the MPC
list2: C. Section 45ZB of the RBI Act, 1934
D. 4 per cent with a tolerance band of 2 per cent either side
questions.explanation: Article 112 covers the annual financial statement and Article 113 the Demands for Grants; the inflation target is 4 per cent (2 to 6 per cent band); Section 45ZB of the RBI Act provides for the MPC.

statements: I. The Monetary Policy Committee has six members, three of whom are from the Reserve Bank of India including the Governor as ex-officio chairperson.
II. The flexible inflation target for the MPC is measured against CPI Combined, with an upper tolerance level of 6 per cent and a lower level of 2 per cent.
questions.explanation: Both are correct: Section 45ZB provides for a six-member MPC with three RBI members and three government-appointed external members, and the target is 4 per cent with a 2 to 6 per cent band on CPI Combined.

statements: I. The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act was enacted in 2003.
II. The Act originally aimed to limit the Centre's fiscal deficit to 3 per cent of GDP.
III. The 2018 amendment allows deviation from the fiscal deficit target by up to 1 percentage point of GDP under an escape clause.
questions.explanation: The FRBM Act dates from 2003 and prescribed a 3 per cent of GDP fiscal deficit; the escape clause permits a deviation of up to 0.5 percentage points, not 1, so III is incorrect.
